transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I feel like I just can’t keep my projects organized anymore, no matter how many lists and calendars I use. It's gotten really overwhelming at work, so I decided it was time to seek some help.

Have you had trouble with organization, focus, or finishing tasks since childhood or your teen years, or did this mainly start recently during a stressful period? Did it happen in more than one setting, like both school/home before and now at work?

Looking back, these issues actually trace back to my childhood, though they became overwhelming after my promotion two years ago. My elementary school report cards often had comments about me daydreaming and having trouble staying in my seat, and my mom got frustrated because I'd start chores or homework and wander off halfway through. So it definitely happened at both school and home when I was younger.

Do these attention and restlessness problems still affect more than one part of your life now, such as both work and home or relationships, and do they cause clear problems like missed deadlines, forgotten bills, or conflict with others?

Yes, it definitely affects both areas. At work, I've fallen so far behind on my project schedules that I was actually put on a formal performance improvement plan, which makes me dread going to the office. At home, I'm constantly losing things like my AirPods or work badge, and I have to work late into the night just to keep up, which leaves me feeling exhausted and out of control.

Have there been times lasting several days when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt unusually energetic, driven, or more impulsive than normal? Or are your focus and organization problems pretty constant over time?

No, my focus and organization struggles are pretty constant and have been since childhood, though they got much worse after my promotion two years ago. When I stay up late, it's not because I have extra energy—it's actually a stressful, desperate effort to catch up on my work. I've never had periods where I felt unusually energetic or didn't need sleep.

Before we conclude this is ADHD, have these attention problems ever been mainly explained by heavy anxiety, depression, substance use, or a medical issue like thyroid problems or sleep apnea? Or do they seem present even when those aren’t going on?

I don't think those other issues are the cause, and to my knowledge, I've never had thyroid or sleep apnea problems. These attention struggles have really just been there since I was a child, even before I had any major stress in my life.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent pattern of inattention and restlessness beginning in childhood, present across school and home in youth and across work and home currently, with clear functional impairment. Symptoms are chronic rather than episodic, arguing against bipolar-spectrum causes, and are not primarily explained by anxiety, depression, substance use, or a medical condition based on the interview.
